privacy_description: What elliotleelewis.com collects about you (very little), who else sees it, and how to ask me about it.
privacy_intro: This is my personal site, and I’m the one responsible for it. I don’t ask who you are, I don’t sell anything, and I don’t track you. Here’s everything the site collects about you, and what happens to it.
privacy_visits_body: Cloudflare hosts the site, so every request goes through it. Like any web host, it sees your IP address, your browser, and the page you asked for, so it can send you the page and keep the site safe from attacks. I don’t keep any of that myself.
privacy_analytics_body: I count visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics. It tells me how many people visited and which pages they looked at, but not who they were.
privacy_board_body: If a run makes the game’s leaderboard and you choose to save it, the site stores your three initials, trees, and distance, for everyone to see. Nothing else is stored with them. They stay on the board until ten better runs push them off. Use any initials you like: they don’t need to be yours.
privacy_turnstile_body: Before saving a score, Cloudflare Turnstile checks you’re a person, not a bot. It looks at your browser, and the site passes it your IP address. Cloudflare uses them only for that check, and Turnstile is only loaded when you save a score.
privacy_others_body: Only Cloudflare, which runs the hosting, the leaderboard’s database, Turnstile, and the analytics for me. Its network spans the world, so your data may be handled outside the country you’re in. The fonts are served from this site, so your browser doesn’t ask Google for them. The links to LinkedIn, GitHub, X, and Instagram leave the site, and those sites have their own policies.
privacy_use_body: Running the site, keeping it secure, and seeing roughly how many people visit. That’s all: none of it is sold, shared for advertising, or used to build a profile of you. The leaderboard only gets your initials if you choose to save a score.
privacy_signals_body: There’s no tracking to opt out of, so the site treats every visit the same, whether or not your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control.
privacy_rights_body: Wherever you live, you can ask me what I hold about you, and ask me to correct or delete it. That includes taking a run off the leaderboard: tell me its initials and score. Depending on where you live, you may also be able to complain to a privacy regulator.
privacy_children_body: Anyone can play the game. It doesn’t ask for anyone’s name, age, email, or location, so it collects no more from children than from anyone else.
privacy_changes_body: If the site starts collecting anything new, I’ll update this page first.

cookies_description: Everything elliotleelewis.com may keep on your device: one cookie from its host, and what the game and the theme picker remember.
cookies_intro: Here’s everything this site may keep on your device, and how to clear it. It doesn’t set any cookies of its own. The only one you might get is Cloudflare’s, which hosts the site, and only to keep it secure.
cookies_privacy_link: What the site collects about you
cookies_cloudflare_body: When Cloudflare’s bot protection can’t tell whether a visit comes from a person, it asks your browser to pass a quick check. This cookie remembers that you passed, so you aren’t checked again on every page.
cookies_set_by_value: Cloudflare, only if you’re asked to pass a check
cookies_purpose_value: Security: telling people from bots. It isn’t used to identify or follow you.
cookies_kept_for_value: As long as the check lasts, 30 minutes by default
cookies_cloudflare_more: Read more in Cloudflare’s own list of its cookies
cookies_storage_body: The site keeps these in your browser’s local storage, so they’re still there next time. They stay until you clear them, and they’re never sent anywhere.
cookies_storage_easter_eggs: The easter eggs you’ve smashed, and how many times
cookies_storage_initials: The initials you last put on the leaderboard
cookies_storage_theme: Light or dark mode, if you picked one
cookies_nothing_else_body: The analytics I use set no cookies and keep nothing on your device, so there’s no banner to click through.
